data.one_liner: Classical Bluetooth serial communication for Flutter on Android.
data.what_it_does: Provides a Flutter interface for Classical Bluetooth via the Serial Port Profile (RFCOMM). It allows monitoring adapter status, discovering devices, pairing, managing multiple simultaneous connections, and sending or receiving byte streams.
use_when: You need to communicate with classic Bluetooth devices like Arduino HC-05 modules or Raspberry Pi over RFCOMM on Android.
You need to manage device discovery, pairing/bonding, and multiple concurrent serial connections.
avoid_when: Your project targets iOS or platforms other than Android.
You need Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) functionality.
strengths: Handles adapter status, bonding, and discovery natively.
Includes stream-based input/output for data exchange.
weaknesses: Limited to Classical Bluetooth RFCOMM / Serial Port profile.
data.setup_notes: Requires Android configuration and permissions, plus ensuring a running SDP pointing to the SP/RFCOMM channel on the target device.
